completeness.reason: The contactor reaction is explicitly delegated ('before any limit is evaluated'), but REQ_CELL_OVERTEMPERATURE is qualified on a *valid* temperature measurement and this element's only validity mechanism is the median of cell VOLTAGES - nothing here (or in any sibling) establishes temperature validity.
completeness.suggestion: State how a cell temperature reading is qualified valid or invalid (e.g. sensor range/open-circuit check, or a per-module temperature plausibility band), so the 'valid cell temperature measurement' qualifier in REQ_CELL_OVERTEMPERATURE has an owner.

consistency.reason: Consistent with ARCH_SAFETY_SUPERVISOR, its sibling on both limit requirements: this element tags invalid, the supervisor ignores tagged-invalid samples, and both run the same 10 ms cycle that ARCH_CONTACTOR_ACTUATOR's 40 ms residual budget assumes.

design_clarity.reason: Names concrete choices rather than goals: daisy-chained AFE readout, fixed 10 ms cycle, mV and 0.1 degC engineering units, cycle timestamp as the budget origin, per-module median with a 250 mV invalidation band.

implementability.reason: Realisable and clearly bounded, but two boundaries need an implementer judgement call: behaviour when an AFE readout fails or returns no data for a cycle is unspecified, and ownership of cell-temperature acquisition overlaps ARCH_THERMAL_STATE_EVALUATOR, which claims to read temperature sensors directly.
implementability.suggestion: Specify the fallback for a failed/absent AFE readout (tag the affected cells invalid, hold the previous sample, or fault out), and reconcile temperature acquisition with ARCH_THERMAL_STATE_EVALUATOR - one element should own the sensor readout and hand valid temperatures to the other.

parent_fit.reason: Fully covers REQ_MEASUREMENT_PLAUSIBILITY (module median, 250 mV band, tagged before limit evaluation) and substantively owns a distinct part of the two limit requirements by acquiring every cell's voltage/temperature and stamping the sample the 50 ms budget is measured from.

summary: Solid acquisition element: fully owns the plausibility obligation and supplies the timestamped, validity-tagged measurements the supervisor decides on. Weak points are temperature validity (the plausibility check is voltage-only, yet REQ_CELL_OVERTEMPERATURE is qualified on a 'valid' temperature) and unspecified behaviour when an AFE readout is unavailable.
